port_instructions: Picker: delete write_relative_jump use. In install_win32_platform_fixes_128: base=(BYTE*)image; cell=(void**)(image+0x01369630); expected=(void*)(image+0x005830F8+1); if (*cell != expected) fail; VirtualProtect(cell,4,PAGE_READWRITE,&old); *cell=(void*)win32_pick_custom_skin_128; VirtualProtect(cell,4,old,&tmp); FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(),cell,4). Optionally memcmp(image+0x005830F8, {2d e9 80 48 0d f1 04 0b 8d b0 6f 46}, 12) first.

win32_pick_custom_skin_128 becomes `static void win32_pick_custom_skin_128(void *platform, void *callback)` (AAPCS, no thiscall). Keep body: adapter=*(void**)((BYTE*)platform+0x3b4); *(void**)((BYTE*)adapter+0xa8)=callback; then win32_pick_custom_skin(NULL, callback). Offsets 0x3b4 and 0xa8 are unchanged. invoke_custom_skin_callback: ((void(*)(void*))(*(void***)cb)[2])(cb) (vtable slot 2, plain call).

ZIP/Directory resource overrides: change typedefs to plain C (no thiscall). Hook = `BOOL win32_128_get_asset(void *self, const GameString *path, GameString *out, BOOL trusted)`. Install by patching cells: 0x0136E598 (ZipPackAccessStrategy[11]), 0x0136E5E8 (ZipPackAccessStrategyOwningFileAcccess[11]) both holding original real_base+0x64E6B8+1, and ADD 0x0136DF2C (DirectoryPackAccessStrategy[11]) holding real_base+0x6314BC+1 (needs its own original pointer; wrapper must call the right one - use two thin wrappers or compare *(void***)self against the vtable address). Read `original` from the cell itself (already Thumb-tagged) after validating it equals the expected function, then store the hook. Accept `*slot == hook` as already-patched like patch_128_zip_slot.

STRING_ASSIGN: game_image+0x00084048 (Thumb: pass (image+0x84048)|1 if constructing a pointer from RVA). assign(output, buf, len) returns output. GameString layout unchanged (inline<16, len@+0x10, cap@+0x14).

Text rewriters (lang_apply_line_override, start_screen_force_development_control and helpers, resource_path_has_suffix, game_string_data, COPYRIGHT/DEVELOPMENT macros) port verbatim; drop the 0.15.10 temp-file functions and fopen hooks.

Xbox sign-in: replace patches_128 rvas by {0x00D99E28,'b'->'!'} (button.signin) and {0x00DA345C,'b'->'!'} (button.xbl_signin), expected byte 0x62; use PAGE_READWRITE (not RWX). Apply before the game constructs its screens/controllers.

TCUI: use cells by NAME not x86 index: *(void**)(image+0x015121FC)=win32_show_profile_card_noop; *(void**)(image+0x01512200)=win32_process_pending_game_ui_noop; *(void**)(image+0x01512208)=win32_show_profile_card_for_user_noop; never touch 0x01512204 (null terminator). Prototypes: ProcessPendingGameUI(BOOL), ShowProfileCardUI(HSTRING,void*,void*), ShowProfileCardUIForUser(void*,HSTRING,void*,void*) all returning HRESULT (E_NOTIMPL for the two ShowProfile*, S_OK for ProcessPending). VirtualProtect range 0x015121FC, 16 bytes.

Do NOT port: write_relative_jump for 1.2.8, show/hide text keyboard, fullscreen command, help URL, achievements/invite no-ops, patch_chat_textbox_compat, win7 patches, 0.15.10 xbox byte patches, unused RVA_128_DEBUG/FONT/COLOR/DEV_VERSION constants.
open_questions: Which strategy serves the vanilla pack in a real ARM deployment? The package on disk has loose files, so DirectoryPackAccessStrategy::getAsset (0x6314BC) is expected to serve lang/start_screen; the zip hooks parity with x86 are kept but may never fire. Confirm at runtime by logging which hook runs for texts/en_US.lang.

Not verified dynamically: that ui/start_screen.json is loaded through the same slot-11 getAsset (lang loading via slot 11 is confirmed statically at sub_5eab30; UI JSON loader sub_129d0c/_ui_defs path was not traced to its slot-11 call).

x86 1.2.8 does not hook showKeyboard/hideKeyboard/fullscreen; if the ARM build needs InputPane/fullscreen shims they must be derived in the imports/winrt area (AppPlatform_Winrt vtable is 0x013695A4; slot 35 = pickFile).

The exact x86 slot index of RVA_128_ZIP_GET_CONTENTS_SLOT was inferred (index 11) from signature/semantics on ARM, since the x86 binary is unavailable; vtable stride 0x50 (19 slots + COL) is consistent with the x86 cells being 0x50 apart.
Callback `callback` object type for pickFile (vtable[2]) was identified only by call shape (adapter+0xa8 then vtable+8); class name unknown.
